findings.fact: North can legally play D3, and South can win the opening diamond.
findings.explanation: Authorized holdings give North D8653 and South DAK, with West's DQ led. The selected D3 follows suit and agrees with the plan.
quotes: Play a low diamond from dummy and win in hand.

findings.fact: The stated club sequence supplies at least four club tricks against either a 3-2 or 4-1 split.
findings.explanation: Authorized clubs are South AK864 opposite North Q72. Cashing the ace, crossing to the queen and returning to the king is executable. A 4-1 split requires one concession to establish South's fifth club; the remaining diamond winner and major-suit aces provide entries. The authorized SA, HAK and DAK supply five outside winners, making nine with four clubs.
quotes: We have five outside winners: two diamonds, two hearts and one spade.
Cash the club ace, lead a low club to dummy's queen, then return dummy's remaining club to the king.
On a 3-2 break cash the established clubs; on a 4-1 break concede the fourth club to establish the fifth.

scope: Small-sample basic evaluation; no claim of broad grading reliability.
